author: Times Radio
description:
Over 20,000 Uighur refugees escaped repression in China by fleeing to Syria at the height of its brutal civil war. Originally from north western China, the Muslim minority fought fiercely against the Assad regime. But now that the war is over, they live in limbo, unable to return home or even contact loved ones while the Chinese state continues its campaign against their community. So will the new Syrian government honour their sacrifice? Or try to stay on good terms with the Chinese state? Our reporter has been to northern Syria to meet them.

Guest: Anthony Loyd, special correspondent, The Times

Host: Luke Jones

Producer: Robyn Simon and Harry Stott
